profile.name: Mankind Pharma Ltd
profile.founded: 1995 (operations); founded 1991 by Ramesh Juneja and Rajeev Juneja
profile.listed: NSE/BSE 9-May-2023 (IPO at ₹1,080, entirely an offer for sale by promoters and private-equity holders)
profile.rankIPM: #4 in the Indian pharmaceutical market by value, 4.7% share (IQVIA MAT Mar-2026); #2 by volume (6.1% volume share); #1 in prescriptions for nine years (15.2% share, Q1FY27); #1 in gynaecology by value
profile.fieldForce: 18,500+ including field managers (AR FY26); ~16,800 in the investor deck; doctor coverage 5 lakh+
profile.chronicShare: Chronic therapies 39% of domestic sales ex-BSV in FY26 (28% in FY18; 38.5% on IQVIA FY26), 40.0% in Q1FY27; target 50% over 4-5 years
profile.geographicMix: Metro & Class-1 towns 56.5% of domestic secondary sales in FY26 (50.7% in FY17, IQVIA); the company describes a 47% presence in Tier II-VI cities and rural markets vs 34% for the IPM
profile.brands: 22 brands above ₹100 cr and 13 above ₹200 cr in FY26 (11 in FY25); top brands Manforce (₹596 cr), Moxikind-CV (₹408 cr), Amlokind-AT (₹300 cr), Unwanted-Kit (₹256 cr), Prega News (₹248 cr), Dydroboon (₹240 cr), Telmikind-AM (₹212 cr); Telmikind family ₹750 cr+; Glizid family ₹230 cr+ (MAT Mar-26)
profile.plants: Integrated manufacturing in Himachal Pradesh (Paonta Sahib), Sikkim, Udaipur, Ambernath (BSV) and Germany (BSV, USFDA accredited); Udaipur and Ambernath EU-GMP certified in FY26; new biotech facility planned in Vadodara

deal.name: Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV)
deal.seller: Advent International (Ansamira Ltd, Miransa Ltd) and two minority holders

bsvFy24.note: EBITDA adjusted for acquisition/exit costs and ESAR

deal.multipleFy24: ~28x FY24 adjusted EBITDA at the ₹13,630 cr enterprise value

ppa.amortisationNote: Not disclosed directly. Q1FY27 call: of ~₹225 cr quarterly D&A 'broadly 50% was allocated towards the acquisition-related depreciation' (~₹112.5 cr a quarter, ₹450 cr a year). Cross-checks: group amortisation of intangibles rose from ₹162.38 cr (FY24) to ₹362.29 cr (FY25, BSV for 160 days: +₹200 cr = ₹456 cr a year) and ₹593.78 cr (FY26).

deal.funding: Internal accruals and debt: ₹5,000 cr of secured NCDs (three series: ₹1,250 cr at 7.99% for 18 months, repaid 16-Apr-2026; ₹1,250 cr at 7.99% due 16-Oct-2026; ₹2,500 cr at 7.97% due 16-Nov-2027; secured by a pledge of BSV shares) plus up to ₹5,000 cr of commercial paper (fully repaid by Q3FY26), then a ₹3,000 cr QIP (1,19,04,761 shares at ₹2,520, allotted 20-Dec-2024) and the ₹562 cr sale of Mahananda Spa & Resorts to Chalet Hotels (Feb-2025) to retire debt.
deal.leverageTarget: Net debt/EBITDA below 2x by FY26 (deal deck); achieved 1.1x at Mar-26 and 0.9x at Jun-26; acquisition debt to be repaid by FY28 (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls)
deal.rationale: High entry-barrier specialty portfolio (recombinant Anti-D, rFSH/Foligraf, HMG, IVIG, equine immunoglobulins, liposomal amphotericin B), R&D platforms in recombinants and complex delivery, women's-health and fertility leadership, a niche international business; synergies from Mankind's reach and MR productivity, OTX shifts and in-sourcing of outsourced manufacturing (not quantified)
deal.antiDPatent: Patent in India until 2028 (deal deck); 100% share of the Indian Anti-D market per management (Q4FY26 call)

fy26.exceptionalNote: Labour Codes (notified 21-Nov-2025): gratuity ₹81.06 cr and leave ₹16.23 cr; stamp duty/costs on assigning trademarks between the company and BSV; ₹13.44 cr write-down of a BSV greenfield project (AR FY26 note 63)
fy26.roce: 12% reported; 41% excluding the BSV acquisition (company definition)

q1fy27.iqvia: Secondary sales +12.7% vs IPM +13.0% (ex-tirzepatide); volume +4.7%; chronic +15.8% (cardiac +19.4%, anti-diabetic +12.7%), acute +10.9%; gastro 13.6% (1.2x IPM), VMN +19.3%, gynaec +12.7%, anti-infectives +3.6%; prescription share 15.2%; new introductions 2.8% of sales vs IPM 4.1%
q1fy27.bsv: BSV +21% (domestic ~17%, international ~25%); Foligraf and Humog +39%, Anti-D +23%; gynaec doctor coverage 37,000 (33,000 in FY25); >80% coverage of IVF centres
q1fy27.consumerNote: Cash-and-carry channel discontinued (it was undercutting general trade); modern trade and e-commerce 15% of consumer sales (11% a year earlier), +38%; Manforce, Prega News and Gas-O-Fast gained share

fy27: Revenue: double-digit growth; domestic prescription double-digit with chronic stronger and acute in line with the IPM; aspiration to beat IQVIA growth (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls)
EBITDA margin 25.5-26.5% (reiterated 30-Jul-2026); gross margin 'upward of 71%' (the 71% is conservative for the West Asia crisis: commodity and dollar costs)
BSV: high-teens growth (domestic ~17%, international ~25% in Q1)
International: high-teens constant-currency growth for both Mankind and BSV
Consumer healthcare: high single digit to double digit from Q2FY27
R&D 2.8-3% of sales; capex 6-7% of revenue (Vadodara biotech facility)
Acquisition-related debt to be repaid by FY28
Chronic share from ~40% to 50% over 4-5 years; hospital business, new divisions (Vistar), underpenetrated states

management.name: Rajeev Juneja
management.role: Vice Chairman and Managing Director; co-founder

management.name: Sheetal Arora
management.role: Chief Executive Officer and Whole-time Director (promoter)

governance.promoters: 72.63% (Jun-2026): Ramesh Juneja Family Trust 20.19%, Rajeev Juneja Family Trust 19.36%, Prem Sheetal Family Trust 14.96%, Sheetal Arora 4.67%, Puja Juneja 2.79%, Poonam Juneja 2.56%, Arjun Juneja 1.98%, Ramesh Juneja 1.66%, Rajeev Juneja 1.57%, others (AR FY26 note 20); no pledge reported
governance.promoterSales: IPO (May-2023) was entirely an offer for sale; promoters Sheetal Arora, Arjun Juneja and Puja Juneja sold 1.62% (64.9 lakh shares, ~₹1,368 cr at ~₹2,107) on 8-Feb-2024 to meet the 25% public-shareholding rule; QIP dilution took promoters from 74.87% to 72.71% in Dec-2024
governance.peExit: ChrysCapital (Beige) and Capital Group funds (Cairnhill CIPEF, Hema CIPEF) sold ~7.6% for ~₹5,589 cr in Dec-2023; Beige sold 2.9% (~₹2,470 cr at ₹2,122.5) on 26-Mar-2024; Hema CIPEF ~0.9% (~₹771 cr) in Jul-2024. No pre-IPO private-equity holder is named among the large holders in the Jun-2026 pattern (GAM reading of the pattern; residual small holdings cannot be ruled out)
governance.auditors: Joint statutory auditors S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP and Bhagi Bhardwaj Gaur & Co.; FY26 consolidated opinion unmodified with an emphasis of matter on income-tax proceedings
governance.taxSearch: Income-tax search under section 132 in FY24; assessment orders made adjustments of ₹1,908.66 cr (₹1,608.60 cr disallowance of certain expenditures under section 37(1), ₹257.13 cr of 80IC/80IE deductions, ₹42.93 cr other); appeals before CIT(A). Income-tax demands in contingent liabilities ₹1,112.94 cr at Mar-26 (₹1,001.73 cr at Mar-25), ₹229.10 cr paid under protest (AR FY26 notes 37-38)
governance.relatedParties: Extensive transactions with promoter-linked entities (packaging suppliers such as Om Sai Pharma Pack and North East Pharma Pack, Penta Latex LLP, real-estate and hospitality entities); ₹338.58 cr of loans from related parties sit in consolidated borrowings (AR FY26 notes 22, 43)
governance.commissionWaiver: Q4FY26 employee costs fell partly because directors waived commission (Q4FY26 call)
governance.src: AR FY26; BSE shareholding pattern Jun-2026 (Screener); Business Standard 8-Feb-2024 and 26-Mar-2024; Medical Dialogues Dec-2023

history.event: Commenced operations; later launched Manforce and Prega News (2007-10), entered chronic therapies (2018-19) and consumer healthcare
Acquired brands of Panacea Biotec (transplant, oncology and other specialty brands), entering specialty
history.impact: Gross intangible assets rose from ₹68 cr (Mar-21) to ₹1,861 cr (Mar-22) (Screener schedule)

history.event: IPO at ₹1,080: offer for sale of 4,00,58,844 shares (~₹4,326 cr) by promoters and private-equity holders; listed 9-May-2023
Private-equity holders sold ~7.6% in block deals (₹5,589 cr)
Promoters sold 1.62% to meet the minimum public-shareholding rule
Agreed to buy 100% of Bharat Serums and Vaccines from Advent for an EV of ₹13,630 cr
BSV acquisition completed (₹13,768 cr); NCDs and commercial paper raised
history.impact: D&A +₹450 cr a year, finance cost from ₹34 cr (FY24) to ₹639 cr (FY26)

history.event: Sold Mahananda Spa & Resorts to Chalet Hotels for ₹562 cr; gain ₹164 cr in FY25 other income
Women's-health generic business of BSV transferred to Mankind (common-control scheme)
Acquired Rivotril (clonazepam) from Roche; Udaipur and Ambernath EU-GMP certified (FY26); semaglutide pen launched (~Apr-2026, in-licensed)

flags: BSV purchase accounting: goodwill ₹6,473 cr (provisional at FY25) and ₹8,253 cr of finite-life intangibles amortised at ~₹450 cr a year, not tax-deductible (DTL ₹1,800 cr unwinds)
Exceptional items: FY26 −₹129.75 cr (labour codes, trademark assignment, BSV project write-down); FY25 +₹164 cr gain on Mahananda sale in other income
Mutual-fund mark-to-market gains in other income (₹64 cr unrealised in FY26)
Tax rate jumps from 16.9% (FY26) to ~25% (FY27) as the Sikkim exemption ends
Company's 'cash EPS' adds back all D&A (₹19.2 in Q1FY27), not only acquisition amortisation (Macquarie challenged this on the Q1FY27 call)
Income-tax search adjustments of ₹1,909 cr under appeal; demands of ₹1,113 cr not provided
